docs.title: Giving ordinary motors a sense of position.
docs.text:
Elijah Koiki's motor encoder subsystem for the 2 DOF Smart Robot Arm Joint Showcase. Four magnetic encoder channels turn the motion of two DC motor shafts into position and direction feedback for a distributed embedded control system.

Explore the schematic → Follow the signal path

docs.title: Project summary
docs.text:
Team 103 is developing a modular, computer-connected control system for a two-degree-of-freedom robotic arm. Custom PCBs add sensing, communication and motor control to basic DC motors rated no higher than 12 V. My board measures both shafts using the teacher-supplied integrated magnetic quadrature encoders, conditions their signals, and uses a PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano to prepare feedback for the main controller. This feedback is intended to support the team's closed-loop motion control and telemetry. See the Team 103 report for the wider system.

docs.title: My contribution
docs.text: I am responsible for the motor encoder subsystem: shaft sensing, RC filtering and op-amp buffering, digital edge conditioning, local power regulation, and the encoder PIC's connection to the main board. Connor's main board receives the proposed feedback link; Walker's motor driver board controls motor power. Encoder firmware and physical integration are the next implementation steps.

docs.title: Block Diagram
docs.text:
Revision D monitors the two teacher-supplied motors through their integrated Hall encoders. Each motor contributes A/B quadrature signals.

  1. The motor driver supplies the red/black 12 V winding leads independently.
  2. This board supplies +5 V and common ground to the blue/green encoder leads through J2/J3.
  3. Four yellow/white A/B signals pass through pull-ups, 1 kΩ / 1 nF RC filters, MCP6004 buffers and HC14 Schmitt inverters.
  4. RB0–RB3 receive the conditioned signals. Firmware counts transitions and determines direction.
  5. RC6/RC7 connect to the team UART through J6: pin 1 TX, pin 2 RX, pin 8 common ground.

A 9 V barrel input, fuse and HTC LM7805 produce the local 5 V rail. The Nano uses VTG with VOFF grounded for external-powered USB operation. See the schematic for pin-level details and PCB Design for fabrication files.

docs.title: PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano
docs.text: Existing DM164150 module; two 1×28 sockets, 2.54 mm pitch, 15.24 mm row spacing. External regulated 5 V enters VTG; VOFF is grounded.

docs.title: MCP6004-I/P
docs.text:
Four rail-to-rail unity buffers preserve the encoder logic swing after the RC filters. All four amplifiers are used.

Manufacturer datasheet

docs.title: SN74HC14N
docs.text:
Four Schmitt inverter channels, with two unused inputs pulled low individually through 10 kΩ. Both phases are inverted.

TI datasheet

docs.title: Power and connectors
docs.text: U1 is the class HTC LM7805, marking 317, selected as TO-220 with 1 IN / 2 GND / 3 OUT. J1 selects the PJ-102AH center-positive 2.1 mm barrel-jack footprint; verify the actual adapter and class part. F1 selects 5×20 mm cartridge clips and a provisional 500 mA fast fuse, subject to measured current and kit compatibility. J2/J3 are four-way 5.08 mm screw terminals, and J6 is a keyed 2×4 2.54 mm IDC header. Do not substitute parts by appearance without checking pin assignments and dimensions.

docs.title: Assembly extras and fit checks
docs.text: A1 needs two 1×28 female sockets plus the existing Nano. F1 needs two compatible clips and one cartridge fuse. JP1 needs a shunt. Add two encoder harnesses, the keyed 8-conductor team cable, mounting standoffs and any required regulator heatsink. J1 is selected as CUI PJ-102AH; the supplied adapter photo does not confirm voltage, polarity or 2.1 mm inner size. Verify the real class parts against the 1:1 print before release. C8/C9/C10 are bottom-side 0805 capacitors. LEDs use custom pin 1 anode / pin 2 cathode footprints.

docs.title: Protected local power
docs.text:
J1 is a 9 V center-positive barrel input, using the selected CUI PJ-102AH footprint. Its center pin feeds F1 and the HTC LM7805; sleeve is common ground and the switched contact is unused. The regulator marking supplied by the student is HTC LM7805 317. Pins are 1 IN, 2 GND/tab, 3 OUT, drawn together on one side. Actual jack, fuse clips and regulator fit must be checked with the 1:1 print. Input, output and local bypass capacitors support the 5 V rail; D1 indicates power.

Nano VTG edge 51 = +5 V, VOFF edge 55 = GND, VBUS edge 56 = NC. This disables the Nano regulator for external-powered USB programming/debugging. VOFF is permanently grounded on this carrier; remove the Nano from the carrier for USB-only operation. Never apply the 9 V input to VTG. See Microchip's hardware guide.

docs.title: Encoder harnesses
docs.text:
Each motor uses one four-position screw terminal, J2 or J3. The encoder attachment on the teacher's motor listing identifies the following functions. Confirm them against the actual harness and sensor PCB before power-up.

Board pin Function Motor wire J2/J3 1 Encoder +5 V Blue J2/J3 2 Common ground Green J2/J3 3 Encoder A Yellow J2/J3 4 Encoder B White Off-board Motor winding + / −, to motor driver Red / black

The encoder attachment specifies 3.5–20 V supply, up to 10 mA, and approximately 0-to-Vcc A/B outputs. 12 V applies to the motor windings; this PCB supplies the encoder at 5 V. Its 64 counts/motor-revolution description conflicts with the listing's 11 PPR. Firmware counts per output revolution must be calibrated rather than hardcoded from either conflicting description.

docs.title: Filtering and digital conditioning
docs.text:
Each input has a 10 kΩ pull-up and a 1 kΩ / 1 nF RC filter: nominal τ = 1 µs and pole ≈159 kHz. The four MCP6004 stages are unity buffers, avoiding the previous gain-1.5 stage's saturation on full-swing logic pulses. HC14 hysteresis cleans the edges and inverts both A/B phases. Direction still depends on harness phase ordering and the firmware convention.

All four op-amps are used. Unused HC14 inputs 11 and 13 each have a 10 kΩ pull-down; unused outputs 10 and 12 are NC. Supply bypass capacitors are provided. The general course analog-gain requirement needs instructor confirmation for this teacher-approved integrated-encoder change; unity buffers are explicitly identified here.

docs.title: Main-board interface
docs.text: J6 is a keyed 2×4 IDC ribbon connector. The user confirmed this mapping: 1 = encoder TX, 2 = encoder RX, 8 = common ground, 3–7 unused. Pin 8 is electrically the same GND net as both encoder grounds, the power supply and Nano. RC6/RC7 use the planned 5 V UART interface and require firmware PPS configuration. JP1 can isolate TX. Main-board logic-level compatibility must be verified before connection.

docs.title: Power Budget
docs.text:
Revision D powers the encoders and logic from the local 5 V regulator. The motor winding supply is separate and is not part of this regulator load.

Load Planning allocation Basis Two encoder sensor boards 20 mA Supplier attachment: 10 mA maximum each Nano target circuitry 50 mA Unmeasured engineering allocation, not a measured maximum MCP6004 + HC14 5 mA Conservative planning allocation; dynamic load depends on edges LEDs, pull-ups and other loads 25 mA Planning allowance, not measured consumption Total allocation 100 mA Provisional With 25% margin 125 mA Design planning load

At a regulated 9 V input, the LM7805 would dissipate approximately (9 − 5) × 0.125 = 0.50 W, plus its quiescent loss. This calculation is not a thermal qualification. Measure actual input voltage under load, rail current, regulator case temperature and startup behavior. Select any heatsink using the real package, ambient temperature and manufacturer thermal data. Do not size the fuse from motor stall current because that current does not pass through this PCB.

The motor listing's 250 mA rated / 1.2 A stall figures refer to each 12 V motor winding, not the encoder supply. Do not reuse the obsolete optical LED power budget. A current class-stock inventory and supplier quote are needed before claiming compliance with the $60/member course budget.

docs.title: PCB Design
docs.text:
The two-layer 100 × 100 mm Revision D routes both motor encoders, power regulation, conditioning, debug features and the Nano carrier. Motor winding current stays on the motor-driver board. The original Revision B and earlier PCB review are preserved locally.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Signal tracks are at least 0.508 mm (20 mil), power/GND tracks 1.016 mm (40 mil), and clearance is 0.381 mm (15 mil). Through-vias are 0.9 mm diameter with 0.5 mm holes. Ground pours on both sides connect the encoder and main-board grounds. C8, C9 and C10 are on the back. Four 3.2 mm mounting holes and a Nano USB access area support assembly.

docs.title: Fabrication and release review
docs.text:
The CAD stackup records 1.6 mm FR4 and 0.5 oz copper per side. The course mill-spec document states 0.059 inch thickness and the assignment requests 0.5 oz; JLCPCB commonly supplies 1.6 mm / 1 oz outer copper. Confirm the instructor's batch-order settings before release. The design's conservative copper widths do not themselves change the manufacturer's selected stackup. Drill output uses Excellon inch units.

Before approval: fit the actual class jack, fuse clips, TO-220 regulator, Nano sockets and connectors to the print; review regulator temperature; confirm the analog rubric exception and stackup; verify 5 V logic compatibility; and complete the real DFM check. Parts and delivered fabrication costs require a current quote and class-stock inventory. The course budget is $60 per team member with the stated class-supplied exclusions. No budget pass is claimed from the obsolete optical-sensor BOM.

docs.title: Team 103 encoder PCB — Revision D
docs.text:
Engineering review design, November 15, 2026. Not approved for fabrication or purchase. Open Team103_Encoder_RevD_EK.kicad_pro in KiCad 10.0.7. Custom libraries are included.

Changes: two integrated motor encoders replace four optical interrupters; four RC/MCP6004/HC14 channels; HTC LM7805 with three pins on one side; unused HC14 inputs each pulled down; keyed 2x4 IDC, pin 1 TX, 2 RX, 8 common GND, 3–7 NC; PJ-102AH barrel input; 0.9/0.5 mm vias; inch Excellon drills.

Motor interface J2/J3: 1 +5V (blue), 2 common GND (green), 3 A (yellow), 4 B (white), according to the attachment on the teacher's exact RobotShop motor listing. Red/black motor winding wires go only to the motor driver. Confirm actual harness against sensor PCB before energizing. Attachment states 3.5–20V and <=10mA per encoder, 0-to-Vcc outputs. Its 64 counts/rev description conflicts with listing's 11PPR; calibrate firmware.

Nano: edge51 VTG=5V, edge55 VOFF=GND, edge56 VBUS=NC. USB debug/programming can be used with external power. Remove module from carrier for USB-only use. Never put input-adapter voltage onto VTG.

Verification: ERC 0 errors/0 warnings; CLI DRC 0 violations/0 unrouted/0 schematic parity; GUI DRC 0 errors/0 warnings/0 unconnected (GUI parity not run; CLI parity checked). 219 static design checks passed. Five default ignored DRC categories remain: missing courtyard, track endpoint not centered on via, tuning geometry, footprint filters, and component type mismatch. No individual DRC exclusions were used. These software checks do not establish correct physical fit, thermal performance, firmware or functional hardware.

Pending before release: - Actual adapter label is unreadable in supplied photo. Verify 9V regulated DC, center positive and 5.5/2.1mm plug; selected PJ-102AH fit is provisional. - Print 1:1 PDF at Actual Size and fit actual jack, fuse clips, TO220 regulator, Nano sockets, IDC, terminals and other components. Selected footprints are explicit parts, not a guarantee class inventory matches. - General course analog rubric requires gain >1 and excludes Hall devices needing no extra conditioning. Teacher approved integrated motors, but scope of that exception for unity buffers needs confirmation. Do not claim unity gain satisfies gain >1. - Confirm course batch-order stackup: assignment 0.5oz per side and Peralta .059in versus common JLC 1.6mm/1oz outer copper. CAD currently records 1.6mm/0.5oz. - JLCDFM requires account login. No successful analysis or DFM proof exists yet. Do not substitute an unrelated screenshot. - Review 5V UART compatibility, IDC orientation, encoder phase/direction and counts/rev. Firmware remains unimplemented/unverified. - Measure regulator rail current/temperature and breadboard/bench operation. 500mA fast fuse is provisional; confirm real load and supplied clips/fuse fit. - Update purchasing quote after class-stock inventory. Old optical BOM prices are superseded. Course budget is $60/member with class exclusions; no delivered-cost/budget pass established. - Obtain student approval before any order. Instructor batch-order process applies. No Canvas submission or order has been made.

Submission folder contains Gerber ZIP and real KiCad screenshot. DFM screenshot is deliberately absent until actually obtained. Canvas also requires schematic and PCB URLs as comments.

Assisted design uses explicitly prescribed individual routes in routes.py; no autorouter. Student should review and understand the design before submitting coursework. Original Revision B and Revision C are preserved separately.

docs.title: Before release
docs.text:
• Check the actual parts against the 1:1 print, especially jack, fuse clips, Nano sockets and regulator.
  • Confirm teacher approval scope for the integrated encoder and unity-buffer analog path, and the instructor's manufacturing stackup.
  • Review real KiCad and JLCDFM evidence for this exact Gerber ZIP.
  • Verify 5 V UART compatibility and physical IDC numbering with the main-board owner.
  • Measure 5 V regulation, current and regulator temperature before connecting the Nano and encoders.
  • Verify both motors' encoder wire functions and pulses per revolution; check clean A/B transitions and firmware direction.
  • Review costs with class-stock exclusions and approve the order explicitly.
